as_read: The label prints a whole fruit extract reading as caffeine-standardized with theanine beside it, and no read trial tests that preparation alone at that amount with a named primary outcome; the nearest low-caffeine extract trial found no benefit.

quote.text: However, larger clinical studies are needed to support this possibility.

proposed_decision_text: The one label, CaffPhenol, prints CoffeeBerry Coffee, Coffea arabica whole fruit extract, at 143 mg, with Caffeine 100 mg under the words standardized to contain, and Suntheanine L-theanine 200 mg. It says the dose holds 100 mg of caffeine. The stored 23312069 gave a single 100 mg dose and reported plasma BDNF up 143% from baseline in 10 people, with no cognition or alertness measured and no primary outcome named. The closest caffeine-carrying trial, 42234539, gave a whole Coffea arabica cherry extract with 200 mg caffeine and 15 mg polyphenols to 12 cyclists and improved time trial work; it names no primary outcome, gives no extract mass, gives twice the caffeine, and tests exercise, a purpose this label does not carry. Trials of polyphenol-rich or decaffeinated extract fall short as a different preparation: 39064791 at 200 mg and 31829793 reported cognitive gains on selected measures and name no primary outcome. 37299382 gave coffeeberry extract standardized to 40% chlorogenic acid at 100 and 300 mg and its authors report no beneficial effect on mood, energy or cognition, but it is not plainly this caffeine-standardized extract, and it names no primary outcome. No trial read tests the extract with theanine. These reads are of abstracts only, and an abstract that names no primary outcome counts against qualifying for no credit.
stop_list: The caffeine standardization is read from the label's row order and text, 'Caffeine standardized to contain', and the 100 mg statement. The label does not give a percentage.
Caffeine and theanine effects can't be separated from the extract on this label.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_weak rests on one 10-person single-dose BDNF change from baseline. The record's material_form says standardized extract, but the stored trial's powder is not described as caffeine-standardized. Same trial backs coffeeberry.
unread_notes: Abstracts only, read together with coffeeberry from one search returning 29, 25 listed. Theanine plus caffeine trials were not searched, since they don't test the extract. If a clinician reads 37299382 as a near match despite the standardization, this moves to null_literature with the same quote as coffeeberry.
